questions.stem: A 30-year-old male patient is admitted to the emergency department with symptoms of drowsiness and inattentiveness. He is a known epileptic and on treatment. His wife said the doctor recently increased the dose of antiepileptic to control seizures effectively. Examination by the treating physician reveals he has an ataxic gait and gum hypertrophy. Which antiepileptic is the patient taking?

questions.stem: A 6-year-old boy is brought to the physician because of a 2-week history of frequent episodes of unresponsiveness. During these episodes, he stares blankly, rhythmically nods his head, and does not respond to verbal stimulation for several seconds. Hyperventilation for 30 seconds precipitates an episode of unresponsiveness and head nodding that lasts for 7 seconds. He regains consciousness immediately afterward. An electroencephalogram shows 3-Hz spikes and waves. Which of the following best describes the mechanism of action of the most appropriate pharmacotherapy for this patient's condition?

options.label: A
options.text: Blockade of Thalamic T-type calcium channels.

options.label: B
options.text: Inhibition of presynaptic voltage-activated calcium channels.

options.label: D
options.text: Inhibition of GABA reuptake into presynaptic neurons.

questions.answerText: Blockade of Thalamic T-type calcium channels.
questions.solutionHtml:
Blockade of Thalamic T-type calcium channels.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 592.

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man comes to the physician for hematemesis and progressive heartburn over the past five days. Ten days ago, he was started on medication to treat a condition that causes hearing difficulties and pain in the lower legs. He has to manage a serious illness. He has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for the past 20 years. Physical examination shows bowing of the tibias. An upper endoscopy shows mucosa inflammation and a 1-cm punched-out ulcer in the distal esophagus. Which of the following drugs is the most likely cause of the patient's current condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Risedronate
  • This patient's hearing difficulties, bone pain, and tibial bowing raise suspicion for Paget's disease of bone. Heartburn, hematemesis, and an esophageal ulcer after initiating treatment indicate drug-induced esophagitis.
  • Option: B. This patient's drug-induced esophagitis is likely due to oral bisphosphonate therapy (e.g., risedronate). Bisphosphonates, which inhibit osteoclast-mediated bone resorption, are the first-line treatment for Paget’s disease of the bone. Oral bisphosphonates may cause erosive esophagitis and esophageal cancer, especially in patients who do not maintain an upright posture for 30–60 minutes after ingestion. Other side effects of bisphosphonates (both IV and oral) include aseptic osteonecrosis of the jaw, atypical femoral fractures, hypocalcemia, and hypophosphatemia. IV bisphosphonates (e.g., zoledronate) may cause an acute-phase reaction with flu-like symptoms 24–72 hours after administration


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 371.

questions.solutionHtml:
Pindolol
